title: Files contract
description: The ai.nimblebrain.files contract: its identity, version, cardinality, its tools with their visibility, unattended marking and schemas, and the closed list of errors. Every tool error is a tools/call result with isError: true whose first text content is JSON {code, error}. A private tool's code is from errors.private. A public tool's code, and the answer to a tool name the server does not have, is from errors.public, and its error begins with that entry's prefix. Beyond the prefix, error is diagnostic. A request refused before any tool runs is the transport's answer and outside this list. Normative rules: contracts/files/CONTRACT.md in the NimbleBrain repository.

public.meaning: An id names no file in the caller's scope: another owner's, another workspace's, a deleted and a missing one answer alike. For move, any one id; nothing moved.
A folder id names no folder in the caller's scope. Nothing was written.
The call contradicts what is stored: a folder name already taken beside it, a folder moved into itself or a folder inside it, a folder deleted while it holds files or folders. Nothing was written.
read named pages of a file whose type has none (1.0 pages PDFs only).
read named pages, and the document's text could not be extracted within the implementation's bounds. A read without pages answers extractedText: null instead.
create's body, decoded, is over the contract's limit (CONTRACT.md §7). Nothing was written.
create named a MIME type outside the allowlist (CONTRACT.md §7). Nothing was written.
tools/call reached a public tool with no workspace or no authenticated identity in its scope.

The arguments do not match the tool's input schema, or a rule the schema cannot state (a body that is not the base64 its encoding names, a folder path with an empty segment); the tool name follows the prefix, quoted. Nothing was written.
No tool by that name, public or private.

private.meaning: A private tool was called by a principal other than host. Checked before the input and the scope, so the answer reveals nothing about either. Nothing was read or written.
The arguments do not match the tool's input schema. Nothing was written.
The call reached the server with no workspace in its scope, or begin_upload, complete_upload or resolve with no owner. Nothing was read or written.
begin_upload declared a size over the implementation's per-file limit. Nothing was written.
begin_upload named a MIME type outside the allowlist. Nothing was written.
complete_upload named no open upload in the caller's scope: unknown, expired, or another owner's or workspace's. Nothing was written.
complete_upload found no body at the upload URL, or one whose length is not the declared size. No record was made; the upload stays open until it expires.
Anything else. The error text is diagnostic only.

folderId.description: Folder to list, by id; "root" for the top level. Omit to list files across every folder. When set, the result also holds the folders inside it.

recursive.description: With `folderId`, include files in its subfolders too. Default: false.

query.description: Case-insensitive text to match in the filename, description, or tags (and folder names).

kinds.description: Keep only files of these kinds, judged from the MIME type (CONTRACT.md §5, Types).

sources.description: Keep only files from these sources: "chat" (attached in a chat), "agent" (written by an agent), "app" or "manual" (uploaded).

conversationId.description: Keep only files attached in or written by this conversation.

runId.description: Keep only files written by this task run.

createdAfter.description: Keep only files created at or after this ISO 8601 date or time.

createdBefore.description: Keep only files created before this ISO 8601 date or time.

tags.description: Filter by tags (files must have ALL specified tags).

mimeType.description: Filter by MIME type prefix (e.g. 'image/' matches image/png, image/jpeg).

order.description: Sort direction. Default: "desc" for createdAt and size (newest, largest first), "asc" for filename.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`, passed back with the same filters and sort, unchanged. Omit for the first page.

id.description: The file's id: its URI is files://<id>.

source.description: Where the file came from. Known values: chat, agent, app, manual. Any other is unknown (CONTRACT.md §5).

conversationId.description: The conversation the file was attached in or written by, or null.

runId.description: The unattended run that wrote the file, or null.

folderId.description: The file's folder, or null at the top level.

ownerId.description: Advisory: the owner the file belongs to.

workspaceId.description: Advisory: the workspace the file belongs to.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last.

pages.description: Read only these 1-based pages of a paged document (a PDF), at most 10 per call. Use it for a long PDF, or for pages past the truncated text. Omit to read the whole text.

maxBytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes of text to answer, across `extractedText` or `pages`. Default and most: 1048576.

extractedText.description: The file's text, when its type is extractable and extraction succeeded; null otherwise, and with `pages`.

truncated.description: Whether `extractedText` stops at the text bound or at `maxBytes`. False when `extractedText` is null, and with `pages`, where each page says its own.

requestedPages.description: With `pages`: the pages asked for, sorted, once each.

missingPages.description: With `pages`: those past the document's end.

pages.description: With `pages`: each requested page that exists, in order.

folder.description: Folder path to put the file in, '/'-separated (e.g. 'Reports/Q3'). Folders that do not exist are created. Omit, or "", for the top level. A leading or trailing '/' or an empty segment is invalid_input.

mimeType.description: MIME type (e.g. 'image/png'), one of: text/plain, text/csv, text/markdown, text/html, text/xml, text/yaml, application/json, application/xml, application/yaml, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, application/pdf, image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp, image/svg+xml, application/zip, application/gzip, font/ttf, font/otf, font/woff, font/woff2, application/octet-stream. A generic or empty type for a known text extension is read as that extension's text type (CONTRACT.md §5, Types).

body.description: File content, at most 4194304 bytes once decoded. Base64-encoded by default; pass encoding: "text" to write `body` verbatim.

encoding.description: How to read `body`. "base64" (the default) decodes it as standard-alphabet base64 (A-Z a-z 0-9 + /) padded with `=` to a multiple of 4; line breaks are allowed, other whitespace is not, and unpadded or base64url (-, _) bodies are rejected. "text" writes `body` verbatim as UTF-8 — use it for markdown, code, CSV, or any content you are composing yourself.

id.description: The new file's id: its URI is files://<id>.

folderId.description: The stored file's folder, or `null` at the top level.
A folder id, or "root" for the top level.

name.description: Folder name. No '/' or '\'; unique among the folders beside it.

parentId.description: A folder id, or "root" for the top level.

manifest.description: The fields to change: `name` renames, `parentId` moves.

name.description: Folder name. No '/' or '\'; unique among the folders beside it.

parentId.description: A folder id, or "root" for the top level.

version.description: The version of this contract the host consumes. The answer holds nothing that version does not define (CONTRACT.md §14).

mimeType.description: The body's type. application/octet-stream for a known text extension is recorded as that extension's type (CONTRACT.md §5, Types); the type recorded is on the allowlist (§7).

size.description: The body's exact length in bytes. The host sends exactly this many.

source.description: The door the body comes through.

folder.description: Folder path, '/'-separated; missing levels are created at completion, as create's manifest.folder. A leading or trailing '/' or an empty segment is invalid_input.

url.description: Where the host PUTs the body. A repeated PUT replaces the earlier body until the upload completes or expires. An absolute http(s) URL and a bearer capability: it MUST NOT appear in a public output, an error, a log or the screen (CONTRACT.md §7).

headers.description: Headers the host sends with the PUT, verbatim, beside its own Content-Length. Part of the capability. The host refuses an upload whose headers name a field it owns (CONTRACT.md §7).

expiresAt.description: When the URL stops accepting a request (RFC 3339): at most 900 seconds after it was issued. A request begun before it runs to its end.
